format: html

## Setup

```{r}

library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)

df <- read_csv(
  "https://bryantstats.github.io/math421/data/all-states-history.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

head(df)
```

## 1For one continuous variable:
##Density

##Histogram

##Boxplot

```{r}
ggplot(df, aes(x = positiveIncrease)) +
  geom_density(fill = "lightblue", na.rm = TRUE) +
  labs(
    title = "Density of Daily Positive COVID Cases",
    x = "Daily Increase in Positive Cases",
    y = "Density"
  ) 

ggplot(df, aes(x = positiveIncrease)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 40, fill = "steelblue",
                 color = "black", na.rm = TRUE) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Daily Positive COVID Cases",
    x = "Daily Increase in Positive Cases",
    y = "Count"
  ) 
  


ggplot(df, aes(y = positiveIncrease)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "lightgreen", na.rm = TRUE) +
  labs(
    title = "Boxplot of Daily Positive COVID Cases",
    y = "Daily Increase in Positive Cases"
  ) 
 
```

## 2- For one categorical variable - Barplot

```{r}

ggplot(df, aes(x = state)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(
    title = "Number of Observations by State",
    x = "State",
    y = "Number of Observations"
  ) 
 
  

```

## 3 For two continuous variables Scatter Plot - Line Plot - Smooth Plot

```{r}
ggplot(df, aes(x = positive, y = death)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3, na.rm = TRUE) +
  labs(
    title = "COVID Cases vs Deaths",
    x = "Cumulative Positive Cases",
    y = "Cumulative Deaths"
  ) 
  

df %>%
  filter(state == "NY") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = date, y = positive)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    title = "Cumulative COVID Cases in New York Over Time",
    x = "Date",
    y = "Cumulative Positive Cases"
  ) 
 

df %>%
  filter(state == "NY") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = positive, y = death)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE, na.rm = TRUE) +
  labs(
    title = "Relationship Between COVID Cases and Deaths in NY",
    x = "Cumulative Positive Cases",
    y = "Cumulative Deaths"
  )
```

## 4 For one continuous + one categorical variables - Density - BoxPlot

```{r}
selected_states <- df %>%
  filter(state %in% c("NY", "CA", "TX", "FL", "MA"))


# Density Plot
ggplot(selected_states,
       aes(x = positiveIncrease, fill = state)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.3, na.rm = TRUE) +
  labs(
    title = "Daily COVID Case Increases by State",
    x = "Daily Increase in Positive Cases",
    y = "Density",
    fill = "State"
  ) 
  
ggplot(selected_states,
       aes(x = state, y = positiveIncrease)) +
  geom_boxplot(na.rm = TRUE) +
  labs(
    title = "Daily COVID Case Increases by State",
    x = "State",
    y = "Daily Increase in Positive Cases"
  ) 
  

```

## 5 For two categorical variables: barplot
 
```{r}
selected_states <- selected_states %>%
  mutate(
    case_level = if_else(
      positiveIncrease >= 1000,
      "1,000 or more",
      "Under 1,000"
    )
  )

ggplot(selected_states,
       aes(x = state, fill = case_level)) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge") +
  labs(
    title = "Frequency of High and Low Case-Increase Days by State",
    x = "State",
    y = "Number of Days",
    fill = "Daily Case Increase"
  ) 
  

```

## 6 A plot that contains three variables

```{r}

ggplot(selected_states,
       aes(x = date, y = positiveIncrease, color = state)) +
  geom_line(na.rm = TRUE) +
  labs(
    title = "Daily COVID Case Increases Over Time by State",
    x = "Date",
    y = "Daily Increase in Positive Cases",
    color = "State"
  ) 
 
```
